newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended off their worst levels in quiet trade on Friday as bullish U.S. producer inflation raised hopes of strong gains on Wall Street later, dealers said.
Golds were flat on a lacklustre bullion.

Dealers said trade on the day had been generally quiet and featureless, with only the U.S. PPI number providing any form of direction on the day after the Dow's rise above the 7,000 mark overnight failed to provide any inspiration.

U.S. producer price inflation fell 0.3 percent month-on-month in January, beating Wall Street economists' forecasts of a 0.3 percent rise and triggering expectations of further gains by the Dow later in the day.
"It has been a very quiet market...We saw some consolidation after a good run this week," a dealer said.
"The PPI figure has just come out in the U.S. and the market seems to like it. That is why we are seeing this turnaround," Johan Marais, director at Societe Generale Frankel Pollack told Reuters.

Despite the day's lethargy, the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said a record 4.5 billion rand worth of shares were traded during this week, surpassing the previous record set in the week ended February 7, 1997.
Gold shares came in for a bit of offshore interest at noon as the gold price firmed marginally but drifted off later, slavishly following the bullion price.
De Beers eased as dealers said a report in the U.S. indicated that its share price could be slightly expensive. De Beers closed 200 cents weaker at 146.75 rand.

Dealers said the market's bull run was expected to continue next week on a host of positive local factors, including a stronger bond market and a steady rand, although much would depened on whether expectations of a stronger Wall Street came through.
The overall index lost 20.8 points to 7,020.7, the industrial index dropped 27.5 points to 8,305.3 and the gold index was up 4.7 points to 1,395.1
Richemont was up 50 cents at 63 rand, SA Breweries added 38 cents to 136.38 rand, Sasol slips 75 cents to 51.25 rand and Sappi lost 90 cents to 39.90 rand.

Near-dated industrial share futures ended easier on a softer rand and weaker U.S. S&P futures, shrugging off Wall St's overnight surge, while gold contracts' movement continued to be dictated by the steady bullion price.

Dealers said the market was showing signs of "indigestion" after too much good news this week. They added that the undertone remained firm but that there was strong resistance at the 8,110/20 level on industrial contracts.
The March all-share contract was last at 6,476/84 from 6,491, near-dated gold contracts were at 983/95 from 982 and industrial contracts were at 8,075/80 from 8,084.
